assessment_membership.source: C3-a authoring declaration (2026-09-26): this target is placed in the V1 placement bank's collocation set by this cut's authoring review. The declaration is made here — no authoring fixture and no external assessment export in this repository places this target, so the membership is this review's own and is recorded as such.

texts.text: To reach a judgement about something after thinking about the facts.

The frame is come to a conclusion, or the more formal reach a conclusion: come to a conclusion about something, come to the conclusion that the plan is too expensive. The verb is come or reach, never make; the article a is required, because conclusion is a countable noun here. A that-clause may replace the noun phrase after conclusion, and about names the subject the judgement is about.

结论 has its own verb in 得出结论, and English does not use make here, so make a conclusion is the first repair; the missing article (come to conclusion) is the second, because the noun is countable inside this frame. The pair worth teaching together is make a decision vs come to a conclusion: the two near-synonymous collocations take different verbs, and learning them as a pair stops the learner from generalising make to every decision noun.

come to a conclusion = form a judgement after consideration (the team came to a conclusion after the meeting). make a decision = decide, with no emphasis on the thinking that led there. draw a conclusion = derive a belief from evidence (draw conclusions from the data), often in the plural and with from. The end of a piece of writing is also called its conclusion (the conclusion of the report) — the ordinary noun, not this frame.
得出结论（经过考虑后形成判断）

pedagogical_profile.rationale: Bands are the C3-a authoring judgement (V1 carries no calibration data): the phrase is regular in meetings, reports and discussion, so receptive value is HIGH and receptive difficulty LOW, but it is one member of a family of decision collocations rather than a daily need, so core utility and productive value are MEDIUM. Productive difficulty is MEDIUM because the verb and the article both compete with a direct translation, and explanation cost is MEDIUM because the useful lesson is the contrast with make a decision. RESOURCE_PRACTICE follows the entity's own declared learning_intent ESTABLISH. Revisit when Calibration100 response data exists.

pack_overlays.rationale: The collocation belongs to the general fluency pack (high-frequency multi-word units), so it carries full weight in that pack's coverage accounting.

It is standard in workplace meetings and written summaries (we came to a conclusion after the review), so it carries most of its weight in the workplace pack; the shortfall records that the pack's own review has not placed it.

example_policy.policy: Present at most two examples per attempt, whole sentences only: the canonical sentence first; a SUPPORTING or CONTRAST sentence only after the learner has attempted the canonical form twice without producing it. Show the verb and the article in place (come to a conclusion, reach a conclusion) and keep the make-a-decision contrast clearly marked as the other collocation, and never present an ERROR_INSTANCE as a model.

typical_errors.explanation: 得出结论 is built with a light verb, and the learner carries the light verb over as make, producing make a conclusion. English builds this noun with come or reach, and the repair is the verb plus its preposition: come to a conclusion.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when a form of make (make, makes, made) stands directly before a conclusion in a clause whose frame is the come-to-a-conclusion unit.

typical_errors.error_pattern: come | comes | came + to conclusion | reach | reaches | reached + (to) conclusion (no article in front of conclusion)
typical_errors.corrected_pattern: come to a conclusion (or reach a conclusion)
typical_errors.explanation: conclusion is countable in this frame, and the article is dropped because the noun feels abstract. English requires a: come to a conclusion. The repair is the article inside the fixed frame, not the verb — and with reach the to is optional, so reach conclusion with neither article nor to is the same slip.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when a form of come is followed by to conclusion with no article between to and conclusion, or when a form of reach is followed directly by conclusion with no article and no to.

detection_policy.policy: Fires only on the learner's own produced English text, and only on a visible surface form: the verb, the article and the noun. No model judgement and no confidence score participates (PRODUCT_CONTRACT §8.1: V1 does not treat a model's self-reported high confidence as an R4 certification). Each rule below states the positive direction it must match; the fixture with the same ordinal states a case the rule must NOT match, so every rule ships with a testable boundary. expected values are NO_MATCH (the shape is absent) and NO_MATCH_BOUNDARY (conclusion is there but it names the end of a text or belongs to another verb frame, so the come/reach frame is not in use).

detection_rules.rule: MAKE_FOR_COME: match when a form of make stands directly before a conclusion, because this noun is built with come or reach.

ARTICLE_OMISSION: match when come ... to is followed by conclusion with no article, or when reach is followed directly by conclusion with neither article nor to (reach takes no to), because the noun is countable in this frame and requires a.

ACCEPTED_REALIZATIONS: do not match when a form of come or reach carries the frame with its article and object (came to a conclusion after the meeting, reached a conclusion about the budget, came to the conclusion that the plan was too expensive): those are the accepted realizations.

CONCLUSION_OUTSIDE_THE_FRAME: do not match when conclusion names the end of a text (the conclusion of the report) or when another verb builds it (draw conclusions from the data), because the come/reach frame is not in use there.

detection_fixtures.text: The team came to a conclusion after the meeting.
We reached a conclusion about the budget.
She came to the conclusion that the plan was too expensive.
The conclusion of the report is two pages long.
